Another sensationalist Daily Mail headline. Propranolol isn’t some mysterious new “panic pill”. It’s a well-established beta blocker prescribed for decades for cardiovascular conditions, migraines and the physical symptoms of anxiety. Like any prescription medicine, it has contraindications and potential side effects, particularly for people with asthma, slow heart rates or certain other conditions. Calling it an “underground sensation” makes ordinary medical treatment sound like a dangerous new craze. Why not explain the pharmacology, clinical uses and genuine risks instead of manufacturing alarm? Medical journalism should educate, not sensationalise.
